checks: Recompute each workload canonical query hash with sqlglot 18.17.0 and compare id, query_hash, exact_hash, source_line against the cache
Compare workload true/PG against source feature float32 labels and cache float64 cards
Compare SQL-derived counts and source feature counts against all cache group offsets
Compare all source feature values against cached values
Recreate every SQL feature in memory with the unchanged vendor extractor; compare all four feature groups and counts against source features and cache
Verify provenance hashes and input size/mtime snapshots
Report rows with errors by database, table count, predicate type and semantic-risk flag; preserve repeated SQL rows in the audit denominator
Recover table-local join-column, filter-column and directional fanout mappings without introducing global database identities

interpretation.alignment_passed: No provenance, identity, label, count or feature discrepancies; full recreation must cover every source row
interpretation.mapping_recoverable: Existing numerical tokens can be mapped back to SQL-local tables and join endpoints; this does not certify the extractor handled predicate semantics correctly
interpretation.semantic_risks: Record join_on, non_equi_join, or, in, between, like, is, neq, not, subquery, self_join, literal_left, malformed_legacy_join, unqualified_column, unknown_column_table, not_join_tree, join_filter_overlap, multiple_filters and non_predicate_column separately. SQL structure recovery, numerically aligned recovery and risk-row totals have independent denominators; table-count buckets are exclusive and predicate/risk buckets overlap.
interpretation.failure: Report the failed rows/databases; do not filter rows, rebuild caches or train on an unverified subset

write_boundary: Only standalone audit reports, logs and PID files; PRICE-master and existing caches remain read-only
post_audit: Decide mapping sidecar feasibility before any implementation. No automatic cache rebuild, model training or target evaluation.
